summary: Presigned-artifact TLS name mismatch caused by split-horizon DNS rewriting S3 host to internal proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports failing model artifact downloads for large model pulls using presigned S3 URLs from their Private deployment. Errors show TLS certificate name mismatch when the platform attempts to fetch artifacts during model load.

Impact:
- Model pulls fail intermittently, causing pod restart loops and degraded inference capacity for the customer's private deployment in us-east-1.
- Affects production traffic for a single customer (FinSolve Analytics).

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peering to Redwood control plane).
- prod/us-east-1.
- Model: gptx-13b-v2 (~4.2GB artifact).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a model rollout that requires a fresh artifact pull (scale up or new node join).
2) Observe model-puller logs in the private deployment agent.
3) Some requests show TLS handshake failures when fetching the presigned URL returned by Redwood Control Plane.

Observed logs (excerpts):
- model-puller: "GET https://finsolve-models.s3.amazonaws.com/artifacts/....?X-Amz-Signature=..."  --> TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed: hostname '10.10.20.45' does not match 'finsolve-models.s3.amazonaws.com'
- curl --location --verbose against presigned URL from within customer VPC shows: "* Connected to 10.10.20.45 (10.10.20.45) port 443 (#0)" then "* TLS: hostname mismatch (certificate is for internal-cache.company.corp)"

Notes from customer: their on-prem DNS resolver and corporate proxy return an internal IP for the s3 hostname (split-horizon) and forward traffic to an internal HTTPS cache/proxy for inspection and deduplication. The proxy uses an internal cert not matching the S3 hostname.
investigation:
Timeline and diagnostics performed:
- 2026-02-28 09:10 UTC: Support replicated failing model pulls in a staging mirror using customer's forwarded DNS rules.
- Ran dig +short finsolve-models.s3.amazonaws.com against the customer's forwarder -> returned 10.10.20.45 (internal cache IP).
- tcpdump from model-puller container showed SYN->SYN/ACK with 10.10.20.45 then TLS ClientHello; server sent a cert with CN=internal-cache.company.corp and SANs not including the S3 hostname.
- curl -v to presigned URL inside customer VPC reproduced: certificate hostname mismatch and the TLS subject contained internal proxy name.
- Verified presigned URL host was the regional S3 hostname as expected; cert returned by upstream connection did not match.
- Control-plane logs confirm presigned URL generation was correct; Redwood side S3 endpoints unaffected.

Hypothesis:
- Customer split-horizon DNS returns an internal IP for S3 hostnames, routing presigned S3 requests to an internal HTTPS inspection/cache appliance that terminates TLS with its own cert, causing hostname mismatch and client-side verification to fail.

Evidence to support hypothesis:
- Packet captures show internal IP and proxy cert CN.
- Curl and openssl s_client show cert CN mismatch when run from inside customer network; same presigned URL fetched successfully from an external network.
- No signs of S3 or Redwood control plane issuing partial redirects or rewriting hostnames.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Customer (Rajesh Kumar): We've observed this intermittently across several nodes. Some nodes succeed, others fail. The proxy team insists they only touch hostnames in a permit list.

2026-02-28 - Support (Nina Patel): Thanks Rajesh — we've captured a pcap and certificate fingerprint. Can you confirm whether your proxy injects a substitute certificate for *.s3.amazonaws.com? Also please share whether you have DNS split-horizon rules for *.s3.amazonaws.com.

2026-02-28 - Customer (Rajesh Kumar): Confirmed: internal resolver returns 10.10.20.45 for bucket hostnames and our proxy performs TLS termination. It's intended for cache/dedupe. We'll escalate to network team to add an exception if recommended.

2026-02-28 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Reproduced in lab with customer's DNS. Verified host mismatch. Short-term workaround: set model-puller no_proxy to include *.s3.amazonaws.com OR add an ACL on proxy to passthrough S3 requests without TLS termination. Permanent: update DNS or use AWS VPC Endpoint (VPCE) for S3 access.

2026-03-01 - Customer (Rajesh Kumar): We added a proxy bypass for S3 hosts and model pulls succeed. We'll coordinate with proxy team to add an explicit passthrough ACL for S3 hosts and update split-horizon rules.

2026-03-01 - Support (Nina Patel): Marking resolved based on customer's confirmation and suggested follow-ups. Created INT-204 to add a runbook note for private deploy customers about split-horizon and presigned URL verification.

2026-03-01 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Noted: recommend adding both documentation and a healthcheck in the agent that validates presigned URL TLS termination path during start-up and surfaces clear error text suggesting 'no_proxy / VPCE / DNS exception' to reduce time-to-fix for customers.
resolution:
Workaround applied by customer: added proxy bypass for bucket hostnames and configured model-puller 'no_proxy' to prevent proxy interception of presigned S3 requests. Result: model downloads resumed and nodes stabilized.

Root cause: Customer split-horizon DNS + corporate HTTPS caching appliance was terminating TLS for S3 hostnames, presenting an internal certificate that did not include the S3 hostname. Because presigned URLs are single-use and host-specific, the client's TLS verification failed.

Permanent remediation recommendations provided to customer:
1) Add an explicit passthrough rule on the proxy for S3 regional hostnames used by Redwood (do not terminate TLS for pre-signed artifact fetches).
2) Update split-horizon DNS so S3 hostnames resolve to AWS IPs or configure the model-puller/service to use a VPC Endpoint (VPCE) for S3 to keep traffic inside AWS without proxy interception.
3) Add a startup healthcheck in the agent to validate presigned URL TLS chain and produce actionable error messages (INT-204 created to track runbook change).

Follow-ups:
- INT-204: Add runbook note and agent healthcheck ticket for engineering.
- Customer will update proxy ACLs and confirm.
